Mitchell carries Natal separately: its `natal` label has nine items 1852-1909 (maize, tobacco, livestock) and NO sugar cane, and its `cape of good hope` label has tobacco only, so the pre-Union cane series exists only under `south africa`, the label every other pre-1910 item routes to the Cape through. The series runs straight into the Union's across 1910 (21,000 ha at 1907 -> 26,000 ha at 1910; 79,000 t at 1909 -> 72,000 t at 1910), and the Union's cane is Natal's. No collision: `natal` has no sugar-cane cell in any year, so nothing is double counted.

STRUCTURAL, FROM AN INDEPENDENT SOURCE. fao1952 `Union of South Africa` horses read 778 thousand at 1937 -- equal to Mitchell's own `south africa` 1937 horses (778,000), which identifies the column -- and 679 thousand at 1950, equal to this label's 1949 figure (679,000) and within 0.5% of its 1950 one (676,000). Mitchell's `south africa` has no horse value in 1938-1958, exactly the years `natal` fills, and the `natal` values run continuously from the national 778,000 (1937) to 472,000 (1959). Natal's own pre-Union count was 40,000-67,000 over 1900-1908. The 1957 `natal` pig value (16,000) sits BESIDE a real `south africa` pig value, so it is not this shape and is not relabelled; it stays unrouted.

PRESENT BOUNDARIES FOR RYE, PRE-WAR FOR FLAX: fao1952's USSR is mixed by item (source_conventions.csv, fao1952/*/*). Its 1934-38 rye averages are 25,870 thousand ha and 25,500 thousand t, against iia `russian federation`'s own 1934-38 USSR (the boundary of the time) 22,790 thousand ha and 20,499 thousand t: 1.14x and 1.24x. Adding what the 1939-45 annexations grew on their pre-war owners' own 1934-38 series (juan: Estonia+Latvia+Lithuania 928, the Finnish cession 28, Bessarabia/N. Bukovina net of S. Dobruja 172, Ruthenia 20, the Polish and German territories 1,923 thousand ha) gives 25,860 thousand ha, which fao1952's figure matches to 1.000 (tonnes 1.07). The same test puts flax fibre on the OLD boundary (0.99x iia, 0.90x with the gains), so no alias can serve the label: rye alone is relabelled to `USSR present boundaries`, which routes back_cast to F228-1945-1991; every other USSR pre-war item stays on F228-1921-1940. Period rows (year null, 1934-1938) are taken because the whole period lies inside the rule. Measured with fao52audit/ussr.py on consolidated_layer_b.parquet, 2026-09-24.

PRESENT BOUNDARIES. fao1952's 1937 USSR `population total` is 188,656 thousand. The Soviet census of January 1939 counted about 170.6 million on the pre-annexation boundary, and 1937 is two years earlier; the Baltic states, eastern Poland, Bessarabia/N. Bukovina and the Finnish cession added some 20 million. The figure is therefore the post-war territory, as the rye series is (see the `rye` rule), and the four 1937 population indicators (total, agricultural, agricultural occupied, female agricultural) share one column. Relabelled to `USSR present boundaries` -> back_cast F228-1945-1991; the pre-war horse, flax and linseed rows keep the `USSR` label and F228-1921-1940.

EXACT FINGERPRINT AGAINST THE RAW IIA EXTRACT (harmonized_data.xlsx), checked 2026-09-24. Nine of the eleven layer-B iia `france` egg-production cells are raw `french saint pierre and miquelon`'s, to the digit: 15.092 t (1931, iia_1933_34), 7.7616 t (1932, iia_1933_34), 5.39 t in each of 1939-1944 and 10.78 t in 1945 (iia_1939_45). Raw `france` prints no production for any of those years, and 15 t of eggs is 0.005% of France's 334,180 t (1937) -- but the islands' own laying-hen count in the same volumes (2,500 heads 1931, 1,200 1932, 1,000 1939-1944, 2,000 1945) gives 5-6 kg of eggs per hen, a real yield, and doubles exactly when the eggs double in 1945. France keeps 1937 (334,180, raw `france`). The 1934-1938 period cell (339,575.39) is the SUM of raw France 339,570 and SPM 5.39 and stays on France: the rule's years cannot take it without also taking France's 1937 row, and the SPM share is 0.0016% (recorded in data_errors.csv, iia-france-eggs-spm-folded-in). No collision: layer B carries no iia `saint pierre and miquelon` label at all.

EXACT FINGERPRINT AGAINST THE RAW IIA EXTRACT, checked 2026-09-24. Layer-B iia `greece` grapes (tonnes) carries raw `italian dodecanese islands` `vineyards: grapes, raisins` production at 1933 (1,600), 1934 (3,300), 1935 (5,600) and 1937 (3,300), all iia_1938_39 -- values two orders of magnitude below Greece's own table-grape crop in the same volume (1936 680,100 = 595,000 + 45,100 + 40,000, 1938 672,500), which stays on Greece. The Dodecanese were Italian 1912-1947 and are not in pre-war Greece (fao1952 prints them separately for the same reason; source_conventions.csv). Two more Dodecanese cells cannot be taken by a year-range rule and are recorded, not moved (data_errors.csv, iia-greece-grapes-dodecanese-period-cells): the 1928-1932 average (3,600) shares its years with Greece's 229,000 ha vineyard-area average under the same item, and the 1934-1938 average (4,500) straddles Greece's 1936 and 1938 rows. ITAEG-1912-1947 has no polygon and is already baselined in validate_data_without_geometry.py for exactly this kind of row; the alternative is leaving an Aegean colony's grapes on Greece. No collision: layer B carries no iia Dodecanese label.

UNROUTED, NOT RELABELLED ONTO A TERRITORY. Checked 2026-09-24 against the raw IIA extract. Every layer-B iia `jamaica` cotton row from 1934 is raw `british west indies federation` from iia_1939_45, not Jamaica: seed (tonnes and ha) equals the raw BWI `cottonseed` rows exactly (1934-1938 2,400 t / 8,000 ha; 1939 2,900 t ... 1945 2,300 t), and lint is EXACTLY 2.00x raw BWI `cotton: ginned` on both axes (1934-1938 1,800 t / 16,000 ha against 900 / 8,000; 1941 3,400 / 20,000 against 1,700 / 10,000). The doubling is in the raw extract, not the source: every BWI `cotton: ginned` row is present TWICE, identical, from the same reviewed sheet (reviewed_163_170_algodon_desmotado_sup_prod_rend.xlsx), and the layer-B build sums them (data_errors.csv, iia-bwi-ginned-cotton-duplicated-rows). fao1952 corroborates the single figure: `British West Indies` 1934-1938 cotton lint 8 thousand ha, 1 thousand t. Raw `british jamaica` prints no cotton after 1927. The rows cannot go to BWI-1833-1962 either: iia `barbados` carries its own cotton lint and seed rows 1934-1945, routed to BRB-1800-2025, and the BWI total contains Barbados, so the whole would be summed beside its part. `british west indies federation` resolves to no polity for iia; this gate checks that it keeps doing so.
